title: University Security & Privacy Assessment Questionnaire
description: A grouped assessment questionnaire covering the institution's cybersecurity, privacy, compliance, and operational security controls.

questions.question: Does your institution have a documented privacy and data protection framework covering how personal data is collected, used, stored, shared, retained, and deleted?
Does your institution maintain an accurate inventory and classification of personal, academic, financial, research, and institutional information?
Are individuals provided appropriate mechanisms to exercise their rights regarding their personal data, and are sensitive personal data given additional protection?
Does your institution enforce role-based access and least-privilege principles for systems and information?
Are strong authentication mechanisms, including MFA where appropriate, enforced for user and privileged accounts?
Are privileged accounts separately managed, restricted, monitored, and periodically reviewed?
Does the institution have a formal process for creating, modifying, reviewing, and removing user identities and access throughout the user lifecycle?
Does the institution maintain an approved information security policy with clearly defined objectives, responsibilities, acceptable use requirements, and leadership support?
Does the institution maintain a complete and accountable inventory of its hardware, software, databases, cloud services, and other information assets?
Is sensitive institutional and personal information protected using appropriate encryption when stored or transmitted?
Are operating systems, applications, databases, and network devices securely configured, patched, and protected against known vulnerabilities?
Does the institution regularly perform vulnerability assessments, security scanning, penetration testing, and remediation of identified weaknesses?
Are endpoints, laptops, workstations, and mobile devices centrally protected using appropriate security controls?
Are institutional networks securely designed and protected using firewalls, segmentation, secure network services, and appropriate traffic controls?
Are remote access and remote working environments protected using secure authentication, encryption, VPN, and appropriate device and network security requirements?
Are cloud services and servers securely configured, maintained, monitored, and protected against unauthorized access?
Are security logs collected, protected, retained, and monitored to detect suspicious activity and support investigations?
Does the institution have a documented incident response process covering detection, classification, reporting, escalation, containment, recovery, and investigation?
Does the institution have procedures for assessing and reporting data breaches or other incidents to appropriate authorities and affected parties?
Are security incidents followed by documented post-incident reviews, root-cause analysis, and corrective actions?
Are critical institutional systems and data regularly backed up, protected, tested, and recoverable?
Does the institution maintain and regularly test disaster recovery, business continuity, and IT recovery capabilities for critical services?
Does the institution periodically conduct cybersecurity and privacy risk assessments and update them when significant changes occur?
Are third-party vendors evaluated before engagement and periodically reviewed for security, privacy, compliance, and service performance?
Do vendor contracts define information security responsibilities, data protection requirements, and incident notification obligations?
Does the institution assess security risks throughout its ICT supply chain and verify the security and provenance of critical components?
Are students, faculty, staff, and other users provided regular cybersecurity and privacy awareness training?
Does the institution follow a controlled process for approving, testing, documenting, and deploying significant system changes?
Are internal and independent security or compliance audits conducted periodically, with findings tracked until remediation?
Are student, faculty, staff, research, academic, financial, and examination records protected throughout their lifecycle?
Are legal, regulatory, contractual, licensing, and intellectual-property obligations identified, documented, and periodically reviewed?
Does the institution maintain documented operating procedures for critical IT and administrative processes?
Are personnel security requirements addressed through screening, confidentiality obligations, disciplinary procedures, and secure offboarding?
Are institutional devices, access cards, credentials, and other assets properly returned or revoked when users leave or change roles?
Are physical security controls implemented for data centers, server rooms, examination areas, records rooms, and other sensitive facilities?
Are sensitive campus facilities monitored through appropriate surveillance or access logging, with anomalies investigated?
Are IT facilities protected against environmental threats such as fire, flooding, power failure, temperature problems, and other physical hazards?
Are IT equipment, cabling, maintenance activities, and physical infrastructure appropriately protected, documented, and periodically inspected?
Are removable media and retired devices securely encrypted, sanitized, destroyed, or disposed of with appropriate records?
Is sensitive information securely deleted or anonymized when it is no longer required?
Is sensitive production information protected through masking or anonymization before being used for testing, training, analytics, or development?
Are data leakage prevention mechanisms implemented to detect, prevent, and investigate unauthorized disclosure or exfiltration of sensitive information?
Are critical systems monitored for capacity, availability, redundancy, and reliable operation during normal and peak periods?
Are source code, privileged utilities, network services, and software installations restricted to authorized personnel and appropriately monitored?
Does the institution use appropriate web filtering and network protection mechanisms to reduce exposure to malicious or inappropriate online content?
Does the institution follow a secure software development lifecycle for applications developed or acquired by the university?
Are university applications security-tested before deployment, including applications developed by external or contracted parties?
Are development, testing, and production environments separated and managed through controlled deployment processes?
Are ERP, LMS, SIS, research platforms, and other critical university applications securely configured, updated, access-controlled, and monitored?
Are security testing and audit activities on operational university systems planned, authorized, controlled, and monitored to prevent disruption?
